gen-dafont-ethnocentric-fs-rowan: Ethnocentric stretches its letters apart, low bowls and short ascenders giving it a fast, aggressive stance on the page. Rowan, a friendly text serif, tucks in underneath with thin strokes and open curves.
gen-dafont-existence-fs-neco: Neco brings a dignified swell from hairline to stem, its letters never pinching shut like a classic serif should. Existence, with its porthole counters, earns its place when big and short.
gen-dafont-existence-fs-recia: Existence is all porthole counters and terminals cut short of the bowl. Recia, a sharp text serif, keeps its modulation faint, so extended paragraphs stay open and easy on the eye at any weight.
gen-dafont-existence-noto-serif: Noto Serif carries a subtle thick and thin cadence and a prominent x-height, literary in a universal way. And Existence matches it with diagonals as sturdy as its stems, industrial where the serif is gentle.
gen-dafont-franchise-fs-neco: Neco is authoritative without stiffness. Its measured swell from hairline to stem lets a classic serif breathe, while Franchise crowds tall small letters tightly together for a strong, clean counterpoint.
gen-dafont-franchise-fs-recia: Tall small letters jammed shoulder to shoulder give Franchise its strong, clean punch. Recia, a sharp text serif with middling stroke contrast, loosens things up below with openings that stay generous.
gen-dafont-franchise-lora: Franchise packs tall small letters against a narrow ascender strip, strong and tightly jammed together. Lora, a bookish classic serif, answers with modest hairline thinning and a broad, welcoming c.
gen-dafont-franchise-noto-serif: Literary and universal, Noto Serif sets the tone here. Franchise is best at strong, clean shapes without calligraphic shading, while the classic serif does its best work through gentle, easing terminals and joins.
gen-dafont-galaxy-fs-rowan: Commanding lines of unbroken width and loose letterfit give Galaxy its cosmic pull up top. And Rowan, a friendly serif, softens the page with gentle modulation and generous curves.
gen-dafont-gobold-fs-neco: Authoritative and dignified, Neco leads with a measured swell. Gobold, with curves that refuse to close and letters spread wide, is best as a bold geometric heading, while the serif suits close reading.
